subject: Territory fragmentation — proposed resolution roadmap and pilot
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego@redwoodai.com>
To: Lina Vargas <lina@orbitanalytics.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodai.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodai.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwoodai.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Territory fragmentation — proposed resolution roadmap and pilot

Hi Lina —

Thanks again for taking time last week. We dug through the pipeline overlap you flagged and sketched a short remediation approach that should minimize partner disruption while protecting active opportunities on both sides. Attached is a first-pass territory matrix (redwood_orbit_territory_matrix_v1.xlsx) and a brief pilot scope doc.

High-level proposal:
- Phase 0 (2 weeks): mutual data sync — reconcile open deals and identify immediate conflicts (we suggest status + ACV + close date).
- Phase 1 (6 weeks): pilot carve-out — execute a 10-account pilot where Orbit stays primary for tooling integrations and Redwood handles inference infra if the customer signs before Sep 1.
- Phase 2 (ongoing): account-routing rules + co-sell credits — agree a routing policy, preserve revenue crediting for introduced accounts.

Open questions we want to lock down in the pilot: who owns pre-sales integration tasks vs. post-sales enablement, and how we handle joint demos for shared opportunities. If this looks reasonable I can coordinate signatures to get the pilot live and route the pilot accounts into a shared tracking board.

Next steps: can you confirm 3 pilot accounts you’re comfortable with and any mandatory compliance items on Orbit's side?

Best,
Diego
Director, Partnerships
Redwood Inference

Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 13:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Territory fragmentation — proposed resolution roadmap and pilot

Diego —

Appreciate the clear plan. Orbit is aligned with a pilot approach; the carve-out timing looks sensible. Quick notes:
- We can surface three pilot accounts this week: Acme Digital, Northshore Health, and TidalCommerce. All three have active POCs and expected close dates in Q3.
- Compliance: we need a brief SOC2 scoping note for the pilot (our InfoSec will want to confirm data flows).
- Joint demos: we prefer Orbit to lead product integration demos and Redwood to be present for infra/cost/latency sections.

Can Marissa own the pilot tracking board and add the three accounts? I’ll get InfoSec started on the SOC2 scoping questionnaire.

Thanks,
Lina
Head of Partnerships
Orbit Analytics

Thanks Lina and Diego — I’ll set up the pilot tracking board in the next hour (Google Sheet + HubSpot shared view) and add ACME Digital, Northshore Health, and TidalCommerce.

Two clarifications from an ops perspective:
- Routing rules: during the pilot we propose the following temporary rule — if Orbit has an active POC (Open/Stage=POC) they remain primary for commercial discussions; Redwood will be invited to win-back or lead infra proposals only with explicit Orbit approval.
- Credits: for any closed-won where Redwood is primary for infra, we recommend a 70/30 split in favor of the introducing partner for the pilot. We can revisit after pilot retros.

I’ll also add a SOC2 scoping checklist tab so Lina’s InfoSec can drop requirements.

Summary of current decisions:

- Ownership rules for pilot: Orbit primary on integrations; Redwood handles infra proposals with revenue-split (70/30 introducing partner).
- Compliance: Orbit to share SOC2 scoping notes; Marissa to add a SOC2 checklist to the board.
- Tracking: Marissa will create shared sheet + HubSpot view; Jonas will add a webhook to push pilot status into Redwood Console for telemetry.

Next steps (by EOD Friday):
- Lina: confirm introduction ownership for TidalCommerce.
- Dan: confirm or deny CloudBridge introduction.
- Marissa: pilot board live and Drive link posted.
- Jonas: webhook skeleton in place (for telemetry).

If there are no objections I’ll send a short MOU to capture the pilot terms and routing rules.

Best,
